parts.label: Part 3
parts.title: All in the family
parts.subtitle: A person’s brothers and sisters can have a powerful effect on their adult behaviour
parts.article:
All in the family

(A) We can choose our friends, the saying goes, but we cannot choose our family of origin. Our parents provide the genetic material and make powerful early role models, but even more influential in determining what kind of adult we will become are our brothers and sisters — our siblings. They occupy a position of unique intimacy in our lives and cast a longer shadow than many recognise or are prepared to acknowledge. By turns, enraging and lovable, familiar and mysterious, our brothers and sisters are the human beings who people our first social relationships. And a sibling relationship is the most enduring relationship many of us will ever have — no less emotionally intense than the bonds we form with our spouses and our own children — if only because they started when we were so young.

(B) Surprising new research by Dr Gene Brody found that having older children who do well in school and are well liked by other children leads to parental ‘basking’ — increasing mothers’ self-esteem. It is clear that in turn this is associated with more positive parenting of younger children, who display fewer behavioural problems as a result. Conversely, parents who get a difficult first child may in turn experience a negative spiral of household tension.

(C) International sports star Piri Weepu is a rugby hard man, but at least some of his tough temperament was forged long ago in the family home. His older brother Billy started rugby — tackling little Piri when he was just four — to ‘harden him up’. It seemed to work. Piri followed his brother in playing for the under-sevens league before he even started school. There are as many such stories as there are families: in the formative hothouse of the family, siblings interact in complex ways with the powerful forcefields of parents, genetics and personality already at work. It starts with birth order, which determines play roles: the firstborn leader, the middle-child mediator and the rebellious youngest. These are roles that can stick for life.

(D) Clinical psychologist Claire Cartwright says she has clients who believe, and it might not have been true, that they were treated differently from their siblings, that one child in the family was preferred over others. They are quite convinced that the parental judgements on them all those years ago were harsher, and that they were the ones who always got into trouble. Later, in the workplace, such a person might be particularly defensive, and so behave in a way more prone to attracting harsh judgements.

(E)However, the research shows that being Mummy or Daddy’s favourite has its own traps. If you were the easy-going, co-operative child at home, you probably excelled at pleasing parents and, later, bosses. But you might, as an adult, find it hard to be assertive with authority figures and lack direction. On the other hand, the sibling who is disruptive and annoying as a child may be able to reinterpret that role later, turning those attention-seeking characteristics into strengths like determination and leadership.

(F) How is it that full siblings, despite sharing DNA, can turn out so differently? One answer is that, in fact, each sibling grows up in a different family, a unique micro-culture. For example, the firstborn is, for a while, an only child, and therefore has a completely different experience of the parents than those born later. The parents themselves are growing up too, weathering hardship or good fortune, so one sibling might experience stability and closeness while another might be raised in the midst of crisis.

(G) Of course, there are many positive aspects of sibling relationships. Annette Henderson, a lecturer in psychology, says firstborn children learn vocabulary more quickly than their siblings because they are not competing to spend one-on-one time with parents. But younger children in turn benefit from unintentional instruction from their bigger brothers and sisters, acquiring entire phrases and an understanding of social concepts such as politeness. Similarly, a Cambridge University study of 140 children found that even when there is a great deal of conflict, siblings will still create a rich world of play and make-believe that extends them developmentally. Love-hate relationships were common among the children, but even those who fought the most had as many positive interactions as the other sibling pairs. It is also true that children compete for parental attention by making themselves different from their brothers and sisters, particularly if they are close in age. A 2003 research paper studied adolescents from 185 families over two years, finding that those who changed to differentiate themselves from their siblings increased the amount of warmth they gained from parents, and also developed stronger personalities and a better sense of their own identity.

(H) Another consideration is that many families today are smaller and more intimate than their historical counterparts. This may be advantageous because siblings tend to know each other better and remain lifelong friends compared to children from bigger or more widely spaced families, who perhaps lose touch with one another after leaving home. Then there was a 2010 American study which found that having a sister, whether younger or older, meant that 10- to 14-year-olds were less likely to feel lonely, unloved, self-conscious or fearful. The same study found that having a loving sibling of either gender promoted good deeds, such as helping a neighbour around the house or helping other children at school.

questions.question: Parents and siblings play equal roles in shaping people’s adult personalities.

analyses.content: 原文明确表示在决定我们成为什么样的人时，兄弟姐妹的影响比父母“更重要（even more influential）”，而非题目所说的“同等作用（equal roles）”
你可能一眼看到前半句肯定了父母的强大榜样作用，但忽略了后半句带有转折意义的比较级，导致误判。
Our parents provide the genetic material and make powerful early role models, but even more influential in determining what kind of adult we will become are our brothers and sisters — our siblings.

questions.question: People’s first social relationships tend to be with siblings of their own gender.

analyses.content: 原文确实提到兄弟姐妹构成了我们最早的社会关系，但压根没有提及这种关系是否倾向于和“同性别（of their own gender）”的兄弟姐妹建立。
你可能看到了“first social relationships”对上了号就急着选正确，但千万要核实题目中像“同性别”这种原文根本没提的限制条件。
By turns, enraging and lovable, familiar and mysterious, our brothers and sisters are the human beings who people our first social relationships.

questions.question: People’s relationships with their siblings tend to receive less attention when they marry.

analyses.content: 原文仅仅将兄弟姐妹的关系和婚后与配偶（spouses）的亲密关系做了一个强度上的同等对比，完全没提结婚后对兄弟姐妹的关注会“变少（receive less attention）”。
你可能看到“spouses（配偶）”一词，就结合自己的生活常识脑补了“结婚后顾不上兄弟姐妹”的情节，但雅思阅读绝对不能自己“加戏”。

And a sibling relationship is the most enduring relationship many of us will ever have — no less emotionally intense than the bonds we form with our spouses and our own children — if only because they started when we were so young.

questions.question: Parental ‘basking’ is advantageous for later siblings.

analyses.content: 原文明确指出父母因老大优秀而产生的“自豪（basking）”感，会促使他们对更小的孩子采取更积极的教育方式并减少其行为问题，这说明它对后出生的孩子确实是有利的（advantageous）。
你可能不认识“basking”这个词或者被长句绕晕，但只要顺着往下一句找，抓住“对小孩子有更积极的养育”这一核心结果就能放心选YES。

Surprising new research by Dr Gene Brody found that having older children who do well in school and are well liked by other children leads to parental ‘basking’ — increasing mothers’ self-esteem. It is clear that in turn this is associated with more positive parenting of younger children, who display fewer behavioural problems as a result.

questions.question: What point does the writer make about birth order in the third paragraph?

analyses.content: 原文表明出生顺序决定了孩子们扮演的角色，并且这些角色会“伴随一生（stick for life）”，完美对应了选项B中“出生顺序可能会塑造成年人的性格特征”。
你可能会被该段结尾提到的遗传学（genetics）一词干扰从而想选D，但原文并没有拿出生顺序和基因去比拼谁对性格的影响力更大。

analyses.content: 原文在描述客户觉得自己童年被区别对待时，特意插入了一句“这可能不是真的（it might not have been true）”，直接说明了这些客户对童年的认知可能是不准确的（inaccurate）。
你可能只看懂了客户在抱怨自己被“不公平对待”，就想顺理成章地选其他关于童年不幸的选项，却漏掉了作者在两个逗号之间那句用来表态的致命否定。

questions.question: What is the writer’s main point about siblings in the fifth paragraph?

analyses.content: 原文清楚地说明，小时候那些调皮捣蛋、招人烦（负面）的特征，在成年后可以转化为决心和领导力等优势（积极），完全对应选项C。
你可能在这一段看到“leadership（领导力）”就直接选了B选项（受偏爱的孩子会成为好领导），但原文恰恰是说小时候不招人喜欢的孩子长大了反而容易有领导力。

On the other hand, the sibling who is disruptive and annoying as a child may be able to reinterpret that role later, turning those attention-seeking characteristics into strengths like determination and leadership.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarises the writer’s argument in the sixth paragraph?

analyses.content: 整段通过举例说明父母的状态和境遇是在不断成长的，所以每个兄弟姐妹虽然在同一个家里，但面对的其实是随时间而变化的家庭环境，对应选项D。
你可能看到段首发问“同胞兄弟姐妹为何大不相同”就想去选C（生来性格就不同），但作者立刻给出的解答核心都在强调外部家庭环境的动态变化。

One answer is that, in fact, each sibling grows up in a different family, a unique micro-culture. For example, the firstborn is, for a while, an only child, and therefore has a completely different experience of the parents than those born later. The parents themselves are growing up too, weathering hardship or good fortune, so one sibling might experience stability and closeness while another might be raised in the midst of crisis.

analyses.content: 原文提到更小的孩子能从哥哥姐姐那里得到“无意的指导（unintentional instruction）”并学到词组和社交概念，这正是选项G中所说的学习经验（learning experiences）。
你可能一直盯着前半句老大怎么学习词汇，却忘了题目问的是“小孩子”和哥哥姐姐的互动包含了什么。
But younger children in turn benefit from unintentional instruction from their bigger brothers and sisters, acquiring entire phrases and an understanding of social concepts such as politeness.
原文指出即使兄弟姐妹冲突不断，他们依然会共同创造丰富的“玩耍和假装（play and make-believe）”世界，这完美同义替换了选项B中的想象力游戏（imaginative games）。
你可能会在后面一句苦找对应词，被“positive interactions”吸引，但真正的答案藏在“make-believe”这个表示假想、虚构的词语替换中。

Similarly, a Cambridge University study of 140 children found that even when there is a great deal of conflict, siblings will still create a rich world of play and make-believe that extends them developmentally. Love-hate relationships were common among the children, but even those who fought the most had as many positive interactions as the other sibling pairs.
原文表示孩子们为了争夺关注会让自己变得与众不同，从而发展出“更强的个性和自我认同感”，这高度概括为选项F中的更大的个体差异性（greater individuality）。
你可能在原文看到了“stronger personalities”就想自己提笔填空，但请务必回到题目给定的选项列表里去找意思最接近的词汇组合。

It is also true that children compete for parental attention by making themselves different from their brothers and sisters, particularly if they are close in age. A 2003 research paper studied adolescents from 185 families over two years, finding that those who changed to differentiate themselves from their siblings increased the amount of warmth they gained from parents, and also developed stronger personalities and a better sense of their own identity.
原文说明因为现在家庭规模小，兄弟姐妹更了解彼此并且能在成年后“成为终身朋友（remain lifelong friends）”，这等同于选项I中的关系更紧密（closer relationships）。
你可能看到“lifelong friends”会在选项里漫无目的地找包含“friend”的词，但要明白“做一辈子的朋友”是对双方拥有“更紧密关系”的一种直白描述。

Another consideration is that many families today are smaller and more intimate than their historical counterparts. This may be advantageous because siblings tend to know each other better and remain lifelong friends compared to children from bigger or more widely spaced families, who perhaps lose touch with one another after leaving home.
原文列举了有姐妹能让孩子减少“孤独、感觉不被爱、难为情或恐惧”等一系列负面心理情绪，这些综合起来正对应选项K中的心理健康（mental well-being）。
填空归纳题最容易犯的错误就是死抠字眼，你可能满选项找“lonely”或“fearful”的同义词找不到而卡壳，其实要把这些词打包向上概括为心理层面的健康。
Then there was a 2010 American study which found that having a sister, whether younger or older, meant that 10- to 14-year-olds were less likely to feel lonely, unloved, self-conscious or fearful.
原文明确指出有一个充满爱的兄弟姐妹能促进做“好人好事（good deeds）”，比如帮邻居干活等，在所有选项中只有D选项的慷慨/乐于付出的行为（generous behaviour）能对标这个意思。
你可能把“helping a neighbour”只看成了普通的体力帮忙，但结合前文的“good deeds”，你必须要在选项中挑出一个能在道德或付出品质上对应的词汇。
The same study found that having a loving sibling of either gender promoted good deeds, such as helping a neighbour around the house or helping other children at school.
